name: Arts and Crafts object
region: Britain, with the United States and Scandinavia
summary: The handmade household goods of the reform movement: oak furniture with exposed joints, hammered copper and iron, stoneware and wool, made in small workshops against the machine ornament of the age.

philosophy.core_thesis: A good object shows the hand and the material that made it: the joint, the hammer mark and the grain are the ornament, and the maker is a free craftsman.
design_principles: Leave each joint in view: a through tenon, a peg, a dovetail or a wedge.
Use oak, ash and elm in the solid, with a straight grain and a wax or oil finish.
Hammer metal by hand, and leave the hammer marks; copper and iron are the main metals.
Use hand-forged hinges and straps of 3 to 6 mm iron on doors and chests.
Put 1 stylised plant motif on a surface, such as a leaf, a tulip or a pomegranate, in flat colour.
Use earth colours: moss green, madder red, indigo blue and the brown of oak.
Make each piece in a small shop, and let a part differ a little from the next.
anti_patterns: Dark, thick glossy varnish that hides the grain
Deep buttoned upholstery with a fringe

form.geometry: Straight, square sections with a gentle taper; a slat, a post and a rail, with a round copper or iron part for contrast.
form.silhouette: A sturdy, upright outline with a broad top rail and a visible frame; a rectangular case on square legs, with a flat lid.
form.edges: A plain chamfer or a soft hand-planed edge of 2 to 5 mm; the hammered metal has a rolled rim.
form.proportion: A settle is about 110 cm high; a slat is about 8 cm wide and 2 cm thick; a post is a square of 5 to 7 cm.
form.ornament: A flat, stylised plant motif in inlay, stencil, enamel or print, and the rhythm of the joint and the hammer mark.
rules: Each frame shows at least 1 through tenon, peg or dovetail.
Each metal part has a hand-worked surface.
A motif is a stylised plant in 1 to 3 flat colours.
Oak and copper cover more than 50% of the visible surface.
A part of one object does not match another part exactly.

materials.rule: Solid wood and hand-worked metal make about 70% of the visible surface; cloth and clay add the colour in earth tones.

finish.gloss: 5–25 GU on wax and oil; 5–40 GU on hammered metal; 3–20 GU on glaze
finish.patina: The style wants a living surface: copper and brass darken in use, wax builds up and a hand mark stays in view.

hardware.section: Straps 20–40 mm wide and 3–6 mm thick; rods 8–16 mm
hardware.joints: Through tenons, pegs and wedges in view; hand-forged strap hinges with round-headed rivets.
hardware.handles: A hand-hammered copper or iron ring, a plain wooden pull or a leather loop, fixed with a visible rivet.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A small switch of brass or copper with a hammered plate and a plain turn knob. A tap is a plain brass cock with a hammered copper basin.

palette.strategy: The earth colours of the material, with moss green, madder red and indigo in the cloth and the clay, and the warm shine of copper.

manufacture.scale: Guild workshops and small firms made single pieces and sets of 10s to 100s.
manufacture.signs: Hammer facets on metal, a through tenon that stands proud, a plane mark on wood and an uneven glaze.

objects.form: hand-hammered copper basin on a wooden stand
small turn switch on a hammered plate (a period-faithful reissue)
hammered copper pendant with a rolled rim
oak sideboard with strap hinges and through tenons
adjustable Morris chair with a plain oak frame
ash chair with a rush seat and a slat back
hand-thrown stoneware service with a matte glaze
wool rug with a stylised flower repeat

positive: Arts and Crafts handmade household object
oak furniture with exposed through tenons
waxed oak with a visible grain
studio product photograph, soft window light

evidence.title: Oak, wood inlay and brass desk

emotion.target_response: Warm trust in an object that a person made: the viewer sees the marks of the hand and feels the care.

use_cases: hardware and furniture for an Arts and Crafts house
a handmade, earthy kitchen or study
a reissue of a copper lamp or an oak settle
a still life of stoneware and copper
avoid_when: The brief asks for sleek, glossy or machine-perfect objects.
The brief needs bright, synthetic colour.

modifiers.how: Add the whiplash line, a flowing floral motif and soft, organic curves in wood and metal.
Remove the motif and the copper; keep maple, cherry and plain oil.
Replace the hand mark with a smooth surface, nickel, glass and pure geometry.

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.
